land.text: all of Balhae: Cliopatria's Liao shape from 926 contains the whole Balhae outline

successors.note: The Khitans took Shangjing in 926 and set up their crown prince as king of Dongdan; Cliopatria ends Balhae in 925 and draws the land as Liao from 926.

land.text: Balhae's land under the Dongdan kingdom (926-936), a Liao dependency

successors.note: Dongdan page: Yelü Bei took the throne at Huhan, Balhae's former capital, in 926; 'Annexed by the Liao dynasty: 936'. A state Cliopatria lacks; it needs a dossier.

capitals.name: Dongmo Mountain (Dunhua)
capitals.note: 'Original capital at Dongmo Mountain (Dunhua)' with no year; used until the Central Capital of 742.

capitals.name: Upper Capital (Ning'an)
capitals.note: '755: Upper Capital at Ning'an'; the page also says a permanent capital near Lake Jingpo was established 'around 756'.

capitals.name: Eastern Capital (Hunchun)
capitals.note: The gazetteer has no Hunchun entry; coordinates are the town.

capitals.name: Upper Capital (Ning'an)
capitals.note: '794: return to the Upper Capital'; it fell to the Khitans in 926.

correction.text: the settlement near Mount Dongmo (Dunhua) and its neighbourhood

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts Balhae in 705 but the page dates the founding to 698 ('Tae Choyŏng declared himself King of Zhen (Jin) in 698, after settling near Mount Dongmo, where he built a walled settlement'). The extent in 698-704 is not on the page: a 150 km circle round Dunhua (confidence 1).

125,330 km2: Jilin and the north of the peninsula (Hamgyong, North Pyongan) up to 43.5 N. The Balhae infobox and text give no area (only 'At its greatest extent it corresponded to what is today Northeast China, the northern half of the Korean Peninsula' and the Russian Far East). The pages give no frontier for 705-740; the southern limit with Silla is unverified.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 741 shape without Liaodong beyond the 705 outline; valid 741-817

keyframe_review.note: 331,752 km2 (+206,000): 292,000 km2 of grid area added between 705 and 741, of which 110,000 km2 is the whole of Liaodong. The Seon of Balhae page has 'Southwest Little Goguryeo in Liaodong' absorbed under Seon (818-830) and the Balhae page has Seon invading Liaodong in 818-820, so Liaodong is removed (except the Yalu corner already inside the 705 shape) until 818; the rest of the growth (north Jilin, Heilongjiang, Primorye edge) is not dated by any page: the Mu of Balhae page has him attacking the Heishui Mohe after 727. Unverified; confidence 1.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 741 shape with Liaodong, from 818

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Cliopatria 741 shape unchanged, from 818, when 'Southwest Little Goguryeo in Liaodong was absorbed into Balhae' (Seon page; Balhae page: 'Sŏn invaded Liaodong and parts of Silla's border' 818-820).

483,524 km2 (+151,800): the Primorye and Amur edge added. Seon's campaigns 'resulted in the absorption of many northern Malgal tribes including Heishui Mohe'; the year is not on the page, only the reign 818-830, so 825 sits inside it.
483,332 km2, the 825 outline; no change dated. The page has Silla fortifying the border with Balhae in 826 and the Khitan conflict beginning in 907.
487,475 km2, the same outline; in 911 'Silla allied with Parhae against the Khitans' and in 924 Balhae attacked the Khitans.

The same outline to 925; the pages end Balhae in 926, when the Khitans 'besieged Shangjing and forced its surrender' (Balhae page) and 'Balhae was conquered in 926' (Dongdan page, no month). Years change only.

ledger.note: 698: Tae Choyŏng proclaims himself King of Zhen (Jin) near Mount Dongmo. 'Tae Choyŏng declared himself King of Zhen (Jin) in 698, after settling near Mount Dongmo, where he built a walled settlement'; infobox 698-926. The Tang named the ruler 'Prince of Bohai Commandery' in 713.

region.text: the Mohe and Goguryeo-remnant lands round the founding settlement

ledger.note: c.705: Balhae grows from its founding settlement to the Cliopatria 705 outline (Jilin, Hamgyong, North Pyongan). The pages date no conquest between 698 and the Tang title of 713; 705 is Cliopatria's first year. A bridge.

region.text: the Mohe lands of north Jilin and Heilongjiang beyond the 705 outline

ledger.note: c.741: Balhae's growth to the Cliopatria 741 outline. The pages date no conquest in these years: Mu (719-737) attacked the Heishui Mohe after 727 (Mu page) and the Central Capital was founded at Helong in 742. A bridge, without Liaodong.
742: the court moves to the Central Capital at Helong.
755: the Upper Capital is founded at Ning'an (the page says a permanent capital near Lake Jingpo 'around 756').
785: the court moves to the Eastern Capital at Hunchun.
794: the court returns to the Upper Capital.

818: Seon takes Liaodong. 'Southwest Little Goguryeo in Liaodong was absorbed into Balhae' (Seon page, no year); Balhae page: 'Sŏn invaded Liaodong and parts of Silla's border' in 818-820; he also 'ordered southward expansion towards Silla'.

region.text: the Heishui Mohe and other northern Malgal lands

ledger.note: c.825: Balhae absorbs the northern Malgal tribes. Seon's campaigns 'resulted in the absorption of many northern Malgal tribes including Heishui Mohe' (Seon page, reign 818-830, no year); 825 is Cliopatria's year. The Primorye and Amur edge.

region.text: all of Balhae, passing to Liao and its Dongdan kingdom

ledger.note: 926: the Khitans take Shangjing and end Balhae. 'The Khitans besieged Shangjing and forced its surrender' (Balhae page); 'Balhae was conquered in 926' and Yelü Bei took the throne of Dongdan at Huhan, Balhae's former capital (Dongdan page). No month on either page; Cliopatria ends the row in 925.

wars.name: Balhae raid on Dengzhou and Tang-Silla counterattack
wars.outcome: Balhae's navy killed the prefect of Dengzhou (732); Mu led troops to Madushan; a Tang-Silla attack was repelled in 733 (Mu page: heavy snow); Silla attacked in vain in 734; Balhae made peace with Tang in 737.
wars.note: The Mu page puts Silla's attack in 733, the Balhae page in 734; the Tang stationed troops in the Paegang region at Silla's request in 735.

wars.name: Seon's campaigns
wars.outcome: Liaodong and the northern Malgal tribes absorbed; pressure on Silla's border (Silla fortified it in 826).
wars.note: No year for either absorption; the reign gives the span.

wars.name: Khitan conquest of Balhae
wars.outcome: Conflict with Liao 'began over Khitan groups near Chifeng and Tongliao' in 907; Silla allied with Balhae in 911, Balhae attacked the Khitans in 924, a Balhae general surrendered to Goryeo and Silla allied with the Khitans in 925; the Khitans took Shangjing in 926 and founded Dongdan.

certainty.note: No frontier is surveyed or fixed by treaty on the pages: the Mohe, Khitan, Tang and Silla frontiers are approximate throughout.

notes: Cliopatria's Balhae (705-925) is a year off at each end (the pages say 698 and 926) and its 741 step is mostly Liaodong, which the Seon and Balhae pages date to 818-820: corrected in balhae_741 (Liaodong removed) and balhae_818 (new). The rest of the 741 growth, and the 825 Primorye and Amur step, are undated on the pages; recorded at confidence 1. The pages do not date the conquests of Buyeo, the Yilou, Yuexi Mohe or Fuyu, a 'Haedong Seongguk' peak, or the 934 refugees to Goryeo. No area on any Balhae page. Tang suzerainty is the Tang dossier's: the Tang named the ruler 'Prince of Bohai Commandery' in 713 and formally recognised Parhae as a kingdom in 762 (Balhae page). Balhae is claimed by Korean and Chinese historiography; family 'korea' follows Cliopatria's neighbours and the claim of Goguryeo succession in Mu's 727 embassy to Japan ('recovered the terrain of Goguryeo', 'succeeded to the culture of Buyeo'); the colour agent decides. Dongdan (926-936) and the Jeongan kingdom of Balhae refugees (no year on the page) need dossiers. Hunchun is missing from the gazetteer (coordinates used). Pages: Balhae, Mu of Balhae, Seon of Balhae, Dongdan Kingdom (4 against a budget of 5).
